a03m.source: author's own essay, supplied by the user 2026-10-03
a03m.subject: CENT #3981 in a slow push-in: the same corroded copper cent, its 1972 date and LIBERTY legend legible throughout, green verdigris pattern unchanged. Camera moves, coin does not. No invented objects, text or second coin.
a03m.rights: motion generated from the user's own still via fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5-turbo/pro/image-to-video
a03m.crop_restrictions: By the last second the push-in crops the coin's rim at the frame edge. Safe as a cover-fitted backdrop; do not use as a bounded plate where the rim must stay whole. Fine patina surface detail subtly regenerates frame to frame — invisible behind a dimmed title, would show at full brightness.
a03m.identified_by: claude, by viewing frames at 0.1 / 1.6 / 3.2 / 4.8s against the source still

a01m.source: author's own essay, supplied by the user 2026-10-03
a01m.subject: The 1971 cent from a01 in a slow lateral drift. Faithful for roughly the first 2.5s; after that the model progressively BRIGHTENS AND CLEANS the coin (+12 brightness at 2.4s, +39 by 4.2s), turning a worn dark cent into a bright pink one. That is the model retouching the object, not moving the camera.
a01m.rights: motion generated from the user's own still via fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5-turbo/pro/image-to-video
a01m.crop_restrictions: Only the first 2.0s are faithful. Staged as a 2.0s forward+reverse ping-pong (4.0s, loops seamlessly) so the drifted frames do not exist in what the renderer can reach.
a01m.identified_by: claude, by measuring mean brightness against the source at 2.4/3.0/3.6/4.2s

trim_pingpong.why: measured brightness drift from source: +1.8 at 1.2s, +6.6 at 2.0s, +12.6 at 2.4s, +38 at 4.2s. 2.0s is the last faithful point.
